Four scalar ORDERS, each a row with its choices, default and a line per choice: STATION (wedge · close · loose · point — where they walk), MESS (the bank · their pack · fast — how they eat), STAND (meet it · hold · quiet — how they meet trouble), VOICE (talk · quiet).

figure.note: the orders read station, mess, stand, voice — twelve choices in all, each with its line and a default

clauses.text: Five PRESETS by name — THE WALKER'S OWN, THE PACK MULE, THE SHIELD, THE SCOUT, THE QUARTERMASTER.

figure.note: the presets read own, mule, shield, scout, quartermaster, each a whole set of orders

clauses.text: Slot geometry per station (three slots each, dealt by index so two backs at one station never share a spot)

figure.note: every station's row holds three slots; two backs at one station stand more than 20 apart at every station

clauses.text: station effects (the looter's reach × 0.7 at close and × 1.35 at loose; a steadier hand at the elbow)

figure.note: the station rows read reachMul 0.7 and 1.35 and a steady at close (the rows' numbers; the reach is not walked)

clauses.text: the HOLD ring (120 px around you)

figure.note: the row reads 120, and under HOLD the knife is met no farther than 126 from the Walker (the ring and a stride)

clauses.text: A hire walks in as THE WALKER'S OWN; a Farkeeper of the kit as THE SHIELD.
STATION is the slot the wedge walks — CLOSE brings both inside 40 px, LOOSE past 90, POINT puts them AHEAD of you.

figure.note: both backs under 40 at CLOSE and at 89.5 or more at LOOSE (a half-pace tolerance); at POINT both more than 40 ahead

clauses.text: a junk drop inside reach stays on the ground with junk OFF; mark it ON and the same back walks over and takes it

THE MESS: their pack eats the ration they carry and leaves the bank whole; the bank draws one provision; a fast draws nothing and the back goes hungry by orders, which is a real trade (a hungry back walks but will not watch yours).

figure.note: their pack: one ration eaten, the bank untouched; the bank: exactly one provision; a fast: none

clauses.text: THE STAND: quiet keeps every hand down — no intercept, no shove; hold screens YOU only (a runner at 200 walks, one at 100 is met); meet it answers at the class's full reach.

figure.record: a runner at 200 walks, one at 100 is met
figure.note: under HOLD the knife walks past the back on point and is met no farther than 126 from the Walker; under MEET IT he is met past 150

clauses.text: VOICE quiet silences the road talk; the calls that matter still come.
Every back keeps a SERVICE stripe — kilometres beside you, crates handled, runners met, sweeps, meals, steadies — and the last thing it did, in its own words.
every back sounds off on the ground, in turn, in the roll-call words ("Tam: on point, holding your back, eating my own.")
They are now wrappers over `effectiveIn / setMarkIn / markStateIn`, each taking the store it reads or writes, plus `seedStore` — a preset landing on a store top-down by the parent law.
Proven: for every item and every verb the pack's wrappers read identically through the parameterized engine, and a mark on a walker's store leaves the pack's ledger untouched.
a gold ghost mark where a back stands RIGHT NOW when it has not reached its slot
